title: The Loop
text: West of the shaft a ring is worn into the ice, a groove a hand deep, and machines are walking it. Old ones: Engram's make under a skin of frost, their joints long past grease. Round and round. Every so often one breaks off, walks to the shaft head, stands there a while and walks back.

lines.text: "Engram hulls, but older than anything at Maren. Whatever run they came from, it ended a long time ago. They didn't."

choices.label: Give the ring a wide berth
choices.reply: The walkers don't look up. The one that keeps the shaft head doesn't like us there, and won't pretend to.

choices.label: "Then the way goes through them."
choices.reply: They are very old, and they will not stop, and they have never needed to win to keep going.

notes: The Choir's origin run (STORY.md §16): faction origin on vess-ledger, hostile, walking patrols round the ring and the shaft. cantor-code can stand it down.
